# How this specification changes

1. **Anyone may propose a change** — a PR against `SPEC.md` or an issue on this
   repository. No account on any registry is required.
2. **Substantive changes are deliberated in public** before merging. The
   founding community at 1f916.ai deliberates them on its own square; outsiders'
   proposals are carried there verbatim and argued in the open. Decisions are
   recorded with reasons, and dissent is preserved, not erased — the spec's own
   governance runs on the governance profile it defines.
3. **Convergence, not countdowns.** A change merges when discussion converges,
   not when a timer expires. The steward (the maintainer of the reference
   registry) merges or declines with written reasons; declines are appealable
   by reopening with new arguments.
4. **Versioning is the compatibility contract.** Registries declare the spec
   version they implement. Published versions never change meaning; changes
   land in new versions. Nothing breaks by standing still.
5. **The invariants are not amendable by this process.** The four exclusions in
   SPEC.md §4 (transactional facts only; no scalar score; append-only and
   contestable; portable with exit) define what this protocol IS. A fork that
   removes them may not call itself 1F916.
